description: One row per collector run: derivatives open-interest / long-short / vol-index snapshot from OKX and Deribit public endpoints, recorded forward because those APIs cannot be paged back beyond their own short windows.
source: OKX public/open-interest, public/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio; Deribit public/get_volatility_index_data and public/ticker -- all read-only, no auth (scripts/record_oi.py)
retention: OKX open interest 1H window ~30 days, 5m window ~2-3 days; long/short ratio ~60 days -- per docs/DATA_GOVERNANCE_PLAN.md this is exactly why this file exists (forward recording is the only way to get a long dense history); snapshot to backtest_data/ at roughly half the shortest source retention

ts_utc.meaning: time this collector run executed (our clock), NOT an exchange timestamp for any individual field below
ts_utc.notes: every other cell in the row is 'best available value from that endpoint at this moment', not synchronized to a shared trade time

okx_usdt_oi.unit: contracts or USDT notional as returned by public/open-interest (see scripts/record_oi.py for the exact field mapping)
okx_usdt_oi.notes: empty cell if this call failed/errored -- rows are best-effort per field, a blank never aborts the row

okx_usd_oi.notes: empty cell on per-field failure, same as okx_usdt_oi

okx_ls_ratio.meaning: OKX BTC long/short ACCOUNT ratio, newest 5-minute value at call time

dvol.meaning: Deribit BTC DVOL index, newest 1-minute close at call time

btc_usd.meaning: OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP last price at call time, added 2026-08-31 to let an entry-price ladder allocate OI deltas to price buckets
btc_usd.notes: rows recorded before 2026-08-31 have this cell empty; those are back-joined from candles by consumers, not filled in here

known_defects: DATA QA 2026-09-05: the largest gap in the 20260905 snapshot (37457s, ~10.4h, ending 2026-08-28T04:22:58Z) coincides almost exactly with the largest gap in schema/venues.json's quotes/trades files and in board_round_series_5s (both end ~2026-08-28T04:18:4[5-6]Z, and the raw WS capture listing shows no data/ws/*.jsonl.gz session starting between 2026-08-27T20:59Z and 2026-08-28T04:18:47Z either) -- this points to the owner's PC itself being down/asleep for ~10.3h that night rather than three independent per-collector failures.

DATA QA 2026-09-05: a second, shorter gap (10568s, ~2.9h, 2026-08-31T09:07:42Z -> 12:03:50Z) is NOT a PC-down event: paper_logs/venues (all venues/pairs), paper_logs/board_round_series_5s (5s cadence held throughout, ~2280 rows in-window) and paper_logs/bot.jsonl (the paper-trading process's own decision log) all show continuous, gap-free coverage across this exact window, and the raw WS session listing (paper_logs/ws_listing.txt) shows a normal reconnect inside the window (session starting 2026-08-31T11:17:22) with no missing block -- the owner PC, network, and every OTHER collector process were up. It is also not a bare external-API outage: scripts/record_oi.py's snapshot() catches every OKX/Deribit call independently and always calls append_row() regardless, writing an all-empty-cell row rather than skipping the row entirely -- so a total absence of rows for 2.9h means record_oi.py itself was never invoked in that window, not that OKX+Deribit were both unreachable the whole time. record_oi.py is one line (after fetch_history.py/fetch_external.py/fetch_okx.py) inside the single sequential deploy/fetch_all.bat, run by the 15-minute 'bitflyer-fetch' Task Scheduler job (docs/OPERATIONS.md SS5) -- the likely mechanism is one fetch_all.bat run stalling on an earlier step (or Task Scheduler's default 'do not start a new instance' skipping the 15-min fires while a prior run was still stuck) for ~2.9h before reaching record_oi.py, which would not touch the independently-running bot/venues/board_round/WS processes at all. This repo has no owner-PC logs\fetch.out.log or Task Scheduler run history to name which upstream step stalled, so the exact culprit step is not confirmed -- but 'PC down' and 'bare API outage' are both ruled out by the evidence above; it isolates to the fetch_all.bat batch (the OI collector's invocation path) alone.
every field is independently best-effort: a timed-out or malformed call leaves only that cell empty and never drops the row -- do not assume all-or-nothing rows

collector interval is whatever cron/task-scheduler cadence is configured (see deploy/fetch_all.bat), not a fixed guaranteed period -- treat gaps > the configured cadence as real gaps, not as a fixed-grid series

OKX and Deribit retention windows mean any row referencing data older than the source's own window (30d OKX OI, 60d L/S) is only trustworthy because it was captured forward in time by this file -- it cannot be independently re-verified against the source after the window rolls
